binary neural networks are not a panacea to the problem of memory and power consumption.
the binary network pruning is a very promising technique for the efficient deployment of binary networks in hardware.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a magnitude based unstructured pruning method, iPrune, that can be used to prune binary networks to a fraction of their size without any accuracy loss, while maintaining their binary nature.

we have designed a new pruning algorithm, iPrune, that is able to prune the binary networks in an unstructured fashion, which is the most efficient way to prune a neural network for LUT-based hardware accelerators.
we have developed a new pruning method for binary networks that reduces the input connections of neurons to only 8.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can prune away the majority of the inputs of each neuron without significantly affecting the accuracy.
the number of inputs can be reduced significantly by pruning unstructured parts of the network, i.e., without changing the network structure, and that this can be achieved without loss in accuracy.
pruning the unstructured connections in binary networks is an effective way to reduce the memory requirements and improve their performance in hardware.
